usage.small_terminal.gb_per_month.rationale: INVESTOR_SET for FY2031, FY2035 and FY2036; SCENARIO for FY2033. FY2031's 5.4 GB is the engineering usage the investor approved (2026-10-04 13:33: "yes, go with the recommended column"; the 4 busy hours, 2026-10-04 19:59: "So for busy hours, it's fine"): 2 Mbps while active, 2.5 percent active at the busy hour and 0.5 percent off-peak, 2.7 GB a month over the 4 busy hours and 2.7 GB over the 20 off-peak hours. FY2035's 8.1 GB is 5.4 GB with the investor's bigger allotment (2026-10-05: "for some of your bigger products, you get a 50% increase in your monthly allotment ... this is just a rough estimate right now"). FY2036's 9 GB (2026-10-12 15:56: "go with 9 GB, 90 GB and 13 bursts"). FY2033's 6.7 GB is about half-way (round 1's 2.7 + 4.0 GB). The words of 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-05 give a usage and a rough allotment, not these totals; the totals became the product case's values with the code design the investor approved at its gate (2026-10-07 13:03: "So actually, I think we're on yes. I think this is yes") and the plan (2026-10-12 20:27: "yes, approved, go ahead with the plan"). The busy-hour part is the engineering usage's; the rest is off-peak.

market.gamma.low.label: Network response, low end

market.gamma.low.rationale: SCENARIO (round 2 of the scratch exploration, 2026-10-06): at 0.5 customers grow as the square root of the network's scale, so four times the network only doubles them. A modeling choice, which no market research grounds; approved by the investor with the product-case code design at its gate on 2026-10-07.

source_refs.note: The Monte Carlo's settings: the network response's range.

market.gamma.high.rationale: SCENARIO (round 2, 2026-10-06): at 1.0 customers grow in proportion to the network's scale, the investor's "If we are getting eight times the network overall, we should be getting about eight times the revenue. That is just an approximation" (2026-10-06); at the range's middle, 0.75, eight times the network brings 4.76 times the customers. A modeling choice, which no market research grounds; approved by the investor with the product-case code design at its gate on 2026-10-07.

market.epsilon.low.rationale: SCENARIO (round 2 of the scratch exploration, 2026-10-06): at 0.5 a price half today's brings 1.41 times the customers and the revenue falls 29 percent. market.epsilon.high.label: Price response, high end

source_refs.note: The Monte Carlo's settings: the price response's range.
Scenario YAML value used for this model run.

market.epsilon.high.rationale: SCENARIO (round 2 of the scratch exploration, 2026-10-06): at 1.5 a price half today's brings 2.83 times the customers and the revenue rises 41 percent. The range is centred on 1, so at the central market, where the headline is read, the price response is exactly 1: for a given usage an uncapped class's price change shows there as customers, not revenue, and a terminal at its seats shows it as revenue; the headline also moves with a price through the usage the pick then takes. A modeling choice, which no market research grounds; approved by the investor with the product-case code design at its gate on 2026-10-07.

formulas.description: Each IoT class's usage in a reported year: its scenario path times the choice's usage scale's line factor, 1 in the first reported year and the scale in the last, in whole messages and bursts, rounded half up.
formulas.unit_behavior: messages a day; bursts a day (whole)

formulas.formula_text: B(t) = m(t) x 340 + b(t) x 100,000 bytes a day, the message and burst sizes the engineering artifact publishes (iridium_physics.iot_message_bytes, iridium_physics.iot_burst_bytes)
formulas.description: What an IoT device sends a day, its messages and its bursts.

formulas.formula_text: v_c(t) = data a month in all(t) / data a month in all(t0) for a terminal; B(t) / B(t0) for an IoT class, at the same choice
formulas.description: What a customer gets in a reported year over what it got in the first, the service term of the demand curve.
formulas.unit_behavior: a ratio to the first reported year (unitless)

formulas.formula_text: a terminal: r_busy = busy GB x 10^9 x 8 / (4 x 3,600 x 30) and r_off(t) = off-peak GB(t) x 10^9 x 8 / (20 x 3,600 x 30) bits a second; an IoT device: uplink bits a second m x 340 x 8 / 86,400 plus its bursts' b x 100,000 x 8 / 86,400 in both periods, or, when its bursts go outside the busy hours, 0 in the busy hours and b x 100,000 x 8 / 72,000 off-peak; random-access attempts a second the same way, one per message or burst; single-tone messages a second m / 86,400
formulas.description: What one customer or device loads the network with in each period: a terminal's downlink rates, an IoT device's uplink bits, access attempts and tone messages a second.
formulas.output_path_pattern: none published: terminal_downlink_use, iot_uplink_use, access_use and single_tone_use read them
formulas.unit_behavior: bits a second; attempts a second; messages a second

formulas.formula_text: busy-hour downlink use = customers x r_busy / (S x r_busy), the seats filled; off-peak downlink use = customers x r_off(t) / (S x r_busy), the load against the busy-hour budget of the same seats
formulas.description: How much of a terminal's own busy-hour downlink budget its customers use, in the busy hours and off-peak.
formulas.unit_behavior: a share of the budget (unitless; above 1 is past it)

formulas.formula_text: a terminal: p(t) / its data a month in all (dollars a GB); minimal-packet IoT: p(t) / (m(t) x 30) (dollars a message); data IoT: p(t) / (B(t) x 30 / 10^6) (dollars a MB)
formulas.description: What a customer pays for each unit of what it gets.
formulas.unit_behavior: dollars a GB, a message or a MB (the cell's unit)

formulas.formula_text: D_c(t) = N_c x k(t)^gamma x (A_c / p_c(t))^epsilon x v_c(t)^eta, with (N_c, A_c) the class's anchor (today's customers and ARPU, COMM-617 and COMM-618; data IoT 999,000 at $15.56 by the investor's proportion, COMM-726) and (gamma, epsilon, eta) the market
formulas.description: A class's demand in one market: today's customers, grown with the network's scale, the price against today's and the service.

formulas.formula_text: a terminal sells floor(min(D, S)); an IoT class sells floor(D), uncapped, its sales checked against IoT's room, access and tone time by the usable test
formulas.description: A class's customers in one market: whole people, never past a terminal's seats; whole devices for an IoT class, always from the demand curve.

formulas.formula_text: revenue_c(t) = customers x p_c(t) x 12 / 10^6
formulas.description: A class's revenue in a year.

formulas.formula_text: F(t) = s x sold_small / S_small + (1 - s) x sold_mounted / S_mounted
formulas.description: The share of the terminals' busy-hour beams their customers fill, each terminal weighted by its share of the beams.
formulas.unit_behavior: a share of the busy-hour beams (unitless, 0 to 1)

formulas.formula_text: Rev(t) = the sum over the four classes of customers x p_c(t) x 12 / 10^6
formulas.description: The year's revenue, the four classes summed.

formulas.formula_text: margin(t) = (1 - C(t) / Rev(t)) x 100
formulas.description: The year's full-cost margin: revenue less the fleet's annualized build and launch cost, over revenue (never called gross).

formulas.formula_text: profit(t) = Rev(t) - C(t)
formulas.description: The year's profit against the fleet's full annualized cost.

formulas.formula_text: U_period(t) = the sum over the two IoT classes of customers x that period's uplink bits a second / R(t), for the busy hours and off-peak; each class's own use is its term of the sum
formulas.description: How much of IoT's payload room its devices use, in the busy hours and off-peak (IoT's room is the whole uplink, the terminals' upload not subtracted).
formulas.unit_behavior: a share of the room (unitless; above 1 is past it)

formulas.formula_text: access use(t) = the larger period's sum over the two IoT classes of customers x attempts a second, over A(t)
formulas.description: How much of IoT's random-access room its devices use, in the busier period.
formulas.unit_behavior: a share of the room (unitless; above 1 is past it)

formulas.formula_text: the larger period's sum over the two IoT classes of customers x attempts a second, over L(t)
formulas.description: IoT's random-access attempts a second a beam, beside the window's 57 a beam (COMM-654) that A(t) holds.

formulas.formula_text: tone use(t) = the sum over the two IoT classes of customers x messages a second x 7 s (the message airtime's high end, COMM-719), over T(t)
formulas.description: How much of IoT's single-tone time its devices' messages use.
formulas.unit_behavior: a share of the room (unitless; above 1 is past it)

formulas.formula_text: G(t) = the sum over the four classes of the GB they carry in a year: a terminal's customers x its data a month in all x 12, an IoT class's devices x B(t) x 30 x 12 / 10^9
formulas.description: The GB the fleet carries in a year for the four classes: bytes add across classes, people and devices never do.

formulas.formula_text: cost per GB(t) = C(t) x 10^6 / G(t)
formulas.description: The fleet's annual cost over the GB it carries in the year.

formulas.formula_text: a choice in one market is usable when, in every reported year, F(t) >= the fill floor, margin(t) >= the margin floor, U_busy(t) <= 1, U_offpeak(t) <= 1, access use(t) <= 1 and tone use(t) <= 1, and Rev(t) rises strictly from each reported year to the next; a market records each test it fails
formulas.description: Whether a choice works in a market: the network mostly used, the margin healthy, IoT within its room, revenue rising.
formulas.unit_behavior: a flag, and the tests failed

formulas.formula_text: the choices in one fixed order: the small terminal's end prices, then the mounted terminal's, then minimal-packet IoT's, then minimal-packet IoT's usage scales, then data IoT's (the last varying fastest); choice_id is the index; data IoT's end price is twice minimal-packet IoT's; a choice is a candidate (at_start_prices) when every end price equals its start price
formulas.description: What the product case may sell, before any market: each end price and usage scale combined, the candidates holding the investor's prices flat.
formulas.output_path_pattern: choices[].choice_id; choices[].end_prices.small_terminal; choices[].end_prices.mounted_terminal; choices[].end_prices.minimal_packet_iot; choices[].end_prices.data_iot; choices[].minimal_packet_scale; choices[].data_iot_scale; choices[].at_start_prices
formulas.unit_behavior: an index; dollars a month; usage multiples

formulas.formula_text: usable draws = the number of drawn markets in which the choice is usable (the usable test applied in each drawn market); usable share = usable draws / draws
formulas.description: How many of the drawn markets a choice works in. The draws' own usable flags are not published, only these counts and the central market's flag.
formulas.unit_behavior: draws; a share of the draws

formulas.formula_text: for each usable test, the number of drawn markets that fail it (a market may fail several)
formulas.description: Which tests a choice fails, and in how many markets.

formulas.formula_text: statistics.median of Rev(t) summed over the reported years, over the choice's usable draws; null when none is usable
formulas.description: A choice's typical revenue over the reported years where it works.

formulas.formula_text: statistics.median of Rev(t1), the last reported year's revenue, over the choice's usable draws; null when none is usable
formulas.description: A choice's typical last-year revenue where it works.

formulas.formula_text: the sum over the reported years of Rev(t) at the central market
formulas.description: A choice's revenue over the reported years in the one market every choice is read in.

formulas.formula_text: sort the choices with at least one usable draw by usable share, then median summed revenue, both descending, then the grid's order; a choice joins the front when its median is strictly above every earlier member's; members are listed most usable first
formulas.description: The choices no other choice beats on both usable share and median revenue (of exact ties the earliest in the grid's order stands for them): over every choice (all_prices, the context: what lower prices would do) and over the candidates (at_start_prices, on which the pick lies).

formulas.formula_text: among the candidates usable in at least the robust floor's share of the draws, the highest median summed revenue, ties to the higher usable share, then the earlier choice (robust_floor_met); when none reaches the floor, the first member of the candidates' front, warned (most_usable_fallback); when no candidate is usable in any draw, no pick (no_usable_choice); usage_edges are the IoT classes whose usage scale is the top of the grid
formulas.description: The adopted case: the investor's prices held flat, with the IoT usage the market supports. What stops the usage: every candidate holds the same terminal prices, so all fail the terminals' fill in the same weak markets; more IoT usage fails IoT's room, access or tone time in more of the filled markets and drops the strongest of them; so the usage rises only while its usable share stays at or above the robust floor and its median still rises, and the floor, the median's peak, or the top of an IoT class's usage list stops it, whichever comes first. A change that moves the terminals' fill or an IoT price can move the usage, in steps. When no candidate reaches the floor, the pick is the most usable candidate, the first on the candidates' front (ties to the higher median), and its usage is that candidate's, warned. On either basis, a pick whose usage is the top of an IoT class's list sits on an upper usage edge (usage_edges), warned.
formulas.unit_behavior: a choice id, its basis and the classes at a usage edge
formulas.scenario_notes: The run never lowers a price: the pick is always a candidate, and lower prices appear only in the front over every choice, as context.

formulas.formula_text: the members of fronts.all_prices at least as usable as the pick with a median summed revenue at least as high, one of the two higher; empty when the pick is on that front
formulas.description: The context choices, at lower prices, that beat the pick: any choice that beats it is beaten or matched by one of these.

formulas.formula_text: gamma = (gamma_low + gamma_high) / 2; epsilon = (epsilon_low + epsilon_high) / 2; eta = (eta_low + eta_high) / 2
formulas.description: The central market, each response at the middle of its range: with the responses drawn independently and uniformly, each class's customers there are its median over the population of markets (in the drawn sample, within sampling error).

formulas.formula_text: the pick evaluated at the central market through the same evaluation as the draws (one market), each reported year's classes and totals by their own formulas
formulas.description: The headline: the adopted case in the typical market, a reading, not a gate (an unusable central market is published and warned).

formulas.formula_text: per reported year and spread field, over the pick's usable draws (null below 9 usable draws, reason too_few_usable_draws) and over all draws: the 50th by statistics.median; the 10th and 90th the exclusive method's first and last cuts at statistics.quantiles(values, n=10)'s indices, with the values sorted x_1 <= ... <= x_c, m = c + 1, j = floor(i x m / 10) clamped to 1 .. c - 1 and d = i x m - 10 j for i = 1 and 9, each cut (x_j x (10 - d) + x_(j+1) x d) / 10 computed exactly and rounded once, so p10 <= p50 <= p90
formulas.description: The spread of the pick's outcomes over the drawn markets.

formulas.formula_text: rank = the share of the basis's draws strictly below the headline value plus half the share equal to it
formulas.description: Where the headline sits among the drawn markets.
formulas.unit_behavior: a share of the draws (unitless, 0 to 1)

formulas.formula_text: for a terminal's customers and revenue: whether the headline sells every seat (customers = floor(S)), and the share of each basis's draws that do
formulas.description: How often a terminal is sold out: where it is, its rank among ties at its seats says little.
formulas.unit_behavior: a flag; shares of the draws

formulas.formula_text: the number of drawn markets, all of them, the usable test not applied, in which the pick's IoT uplink use in the busy hours or off-peak, its access use or its single-tone use is above 1 in at least one reported year (a market counts once)
formulas.description: The all-draw basis's label: in how many markets the pick sells IoT past its uplink, access or single-tone room, markets the usable draws leave out; the basis record publishes the label, the drawn markets and that count.

formulas.formula_text: the number of the run's input cells in each source status, by common.meta.summarize_source_statuses over every input cell
formulas.description: How the run's inputs are sourced: a count of input cells per status, certified, scenario and derived estimates among them.

assumptions: Each class's customers come from the demand curve D = N x k^gamma x (A / p)^epsilon x v^eta, anchored on Iridium's customers and ARPU today (COMM-617, COMM-618): the small terminal 402,000 at $47, the mounted terminal 16,100 at $259, minimal-packet IoT 1,998,000 at $7.78 (Iridium's one reported commercial IoT segment, taken whole).

Data IoT is anchored beside that segment at the investor's proportion (2026-10-04), half the count at double the ARPU, 999,000 at $15.56 (COMM-726), so the two IoT classes start from twice Iridium's IoT revenue today, a run rate at today's count and ARPU ($373.1M a year against $186.5M).
The network's scale k is the terminals' seats over Iridium's 418,100 terminal customers today, the seats read from the engineering artifact: k = 7.8 in FY2031 and 46.6 in FY2036.
The prices are held flat in nominal dollars at the scenario's start prices (the small terminal $10, the mounted terminal $50, minimal-packet IoT $3, data IoT $6); inflation is not modeled.

The market's three responses are drawn independently and uniformly over their ranges (gamma 0.5 to 1, epsilon 0.5 to 1.5, eta 0 to 0.5; 2,000 draws, seed 20261006), so each class's customers at the central market are its median over the population of markets and, in the 2,000 drawn markets, within sampling error of it.

IoT is uncapped: each IoT class sells every device its demand curve gives, bounded by its uplink room, its random access and its single-tone time, which the usable test checks; no IoT count is ever set.

What stops the usage: the pick's IoT usage rises while its median summed revenue rises and its usable draws stay at or above the robust floor's 1,500 (75 percent of the draws), and stops at whichever comes first: that floor, the median's peak, or the top of an IoT class's usage list, where the pick then sits on an upper usage edge, warned; every candidate shares the terminals' fill, so IoT's own failures may take only the draws between the fill's share and that floor. This run's pick: minimal-packet IoT x8 and data IoT x1, usable in 1,744 of 2,000 draws (robust_floor_met).

Each IoT class's usage and time basis differ from the engineering capacity's: the engineering artifact counts each class's devices alone at its reference usage, averaged over the day; the product case sells at the pick's usage by period (768 messages a day for minimal-packet IoT and 13 bursts a day for data IoT in FY2036), so its devices are never divided by that capacity.

IoT's room rides the phone class's useful beams, the beams lit over inhabited cells: 19,160 in FY2031 and 112,065 in FY2036, read from the engineering artifact. So the room counts no beam over oceans or empty land, a conservative basis: the beams there are upside the case does not count. On its beams the room is the whole uplink in its share of the frame after the MAC efficiency, with the random-access window and the single-tone room; the terminals' own upload is not subtracted.
The all-draw spreads cover every drawn market, the usable test not applied: in 73 of the 2,000 drawn markets the pick sells IoT past its uplink, access or single-tone room in some reported year.
People and devices are never added: no total of customers is published; bytes add across the classes in the GB carried.
Government is left out of revenue.
